title.en: Faraday's experiments, magnetic flux and Faraday's law
title.kn: ಫ್ಯಾರಡೆಯ ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು, ಕಾಂತೀಯ ಅಭಿವಾಹ ಮತ್ತು ಫ್ಯಾರಡೆ ನಿಯಮ

hook.en: Push a magnet into a coil and a galvanometer kicks. Hold it still and nothing happens. Only a changing magnetic flux makes a current, and every power station runs on this idea.
hook.kn: ಸುರುಳಿಯೊಳಗೆ ಕಾಂತವನ್ನು ತಳ್ಳಿದರೆ ಗ್ಯಾಲ್ವನೋಮೀಟರ್ ವಿಚಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಸ್ಥಿರವಾಗಿ ಹಿಡಿದರೆ ಏನೂ ಆಗುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ಬದಲಾಗುವ ಕಾಂತೀಯ ಅಭಿವಾಹ ಮಾತ್ರ ಪ್ರವಾಹ ಉಂಟುಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ; ಪ್ರತಿ ವಿದ್ಯುತ್ ಕೇಂದ್ರ ಇದೇ ತತ್ವದ ಮೇಲೆ ನಡೆಯುತ್ತದೆ.

objectives.en: Find magnetic flux through a coil.

narration.en: Push a magnet into a coil and a galvanometer kicks. Hold it still and nothing happens. Only a changing magnetic flux makes a current, and every power station runs on this idea.
narration.kn: ಸುರುಳಿಯೊಳಗೆ ಕಾಂತವನ್ನು ತಳ್ಳಿದರೆ ಗ್ಯಾಲ್ವನೋಮೀಟರ್ ವಿಚಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಸ್ಥಿರವಾಗಿ ಹಿಡಿದರೆ ಏನೂ ಆಗುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ಬದಲಾಗುವ ಕಾಂತೀಯ ಅಭಿವಾಹ ಮಾತ್ರ ಪ್ರವಾಹ ಉಂಟುಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ; ಪ್ರತಿ ವಿದ್ಯುತ್ ಕೇಂದ್ರ ಇದೇ ತತ್ವದ ಮೇಲೆ ನಡೆಯುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: The magnetic flux through a plane area A in a uniform field B is $\Phi_B = BA\cos\theta$, θ being the angle between B and the normal to the area. Unit: weber (1 Wb = 1 T m²). The flux can change if B changes, if the area changes, or if the coil turns (θ changes).
body.kn: ಕಾಂತೀಯ ಅಭಿವಾಹ Φ = BA cosθ, ಏಕಮಾನ ವೆಬರ್. B, A ಅಥವಾ θ ಬದಲಾದರೆ ಅಭಿವಾಹ ಬದಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

points.en: Change B, A or θ to change Φ

narration.en: Magnetic flux is B times A times cos theta, measured in weber. It changes when the field, the area or the angle changes.
narration.kn: ಕಾಂತೀಯ ಅಭಿವಾಹ Φ = BA cosθ, ಏಕಮಾನ ವೆಬರ್. B, A ಅಥವಾ θ ಬದಲಾದರೆ ಅಭಿವಾಹ ಬದಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

title.en: On the board: flux and Faraday's law

narration.en: Push a magnet into a coil: the galvanometer kicks while the magnet moves, and stops when it stops. The magnetic flux through a loop is Φ = BA cos θ, measured in weber. Faraday's law: the induced emf equals the rate of change of flux linkage, ε = −N dΦ/dt. If the flux rises steadily for a while and then stays constant... ...the emf is constant while the flux changes, and zero once it stops changing. Example: 50 turns of area 0.02 m², with B falling from 0.4 T to zero in 0.1 s, give ε = 50 × 0.02 × 0.4 / 0.1 = 4 V.

say.en: Push a magnet into a coil: the galvanometer kicks while the magnet moves, and stops when it stops.
The magnetic flux through a loop is Φ = BA cos θ, measured in weber.
Faraday's law: the induced emf equals the rate of change of flux linkage, ε = −N dΦ/dt.
If the flux rises steadily for a while and then stays constant...
...the emf is constant while the flux changes, and zero once it stops changing.
Example: 50 turns of area 0.02 m², with B falling from 0.4 T to zero in 0.1 s, give ε = 50 × 0.02 × 0.4 / 0.1 = 4 V.

body.en: Faraday and Henry found that a current is induced in a coil whenever the magnetic flux through it changes: when a magnet moves relative to the coil, or when the current in a nearby coil is switched on, off or changed. Faraday's law: the induced emf equals the rate of change of flux. For a coil of N turns, $\varepsilon = -N\,d\Phi_B/dt$. The minus sign expresses Lenz's law.
body.kn: ಸುರುಳಿಯ ಮೂಲಕ ಅಭಿವಾಹ ಬದಲಾದಾಗಲೆಲ್ಲಾ ವಿ.ಚಾ.ಬ. ಪ್ರೇರಿತವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ: ε = −N dΦ/dt. ಋಣ ಚಿಹ್ನೆ ಲೆನ್ಜ್ ನಿಯಮ.

points.en: Moving magnet or changing current nearby → induced current
No change in flux → no emf

narration.en: Whenever the flux through a coil changes, an emf is induced. Its size is the number of turns times the rate of change of flux. The minus sign is Lenz's law.
narration.kn: ಸುರುಳಿಯ ಮೂಲಕ ಅಭಿವಾಹ ಬದಲಾದಾಗಲೆಲ್ಲಾ ವಿ.ಚಾ.ಬ. ಪ್ರೇರಿತವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ: ε = −N dΦ/dt. ಋಣ ಚಿಹ್ನೆ ಲೆನ್ಜ್ ನಿಯಮ.

caption.en: A coil of N turns and area A sits in a field B that is switched off in a time Δt. The average emf is NBA/Δt; faster switching gives a bigger emf.

tryThis.en: Now look at the charge that flows: it does not depend on Δt at all, only on the change in flux.
Double N: twice the emf, because every turn adds its own.

narration.en: A coil of N turns and area A sits in a field B that is switched off in a time Δt. The average emf is NBA/Δt; faster switching gives a bigger emf. Halve Δt: the emf doubles. Now look at the charge that flows: it does not depend on Δt at all, only on the change in flux. Double N: twice the emf, because every turn adds its own.

caption.en: Move a bar magnet in and out of a coil and watch the bulb and the voltmeter respond.

tryThis.en: Push the magnet into the coil slowly, then quickly: the faster the flux changes, the brighter the bulb.
Hold the magnet still inside the coil: no change of flux, no emf.
Switch to the two-loop coil: twice the turns, a bigger emf for the same motion.

narration.en: Move a bar magnet in and out of a coil and watch the bulb and the voltmeter respond. Push the magnet into the coil slowly, then quickly: the faster the flux changes, the brighter the bulb. Hold the magnet still inside the coil: no change of flux, no emf. Switch to the two-loop coil: twice the turns, a bigger emf for the same motion.

problem.en: A square loop of side 10 cm and resistance 0.5 Ω is in a uniform field of 0.10 T at 45° to its normal. The field is reduced steadily to zero in 0.70 s. Find the induced emf and current.

steps.en: Initial flux Φ = BA cos 45° = 0.1 × 0.01 × 0.707 = 7.07 × 10⁻⁴ Wb.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A square loop of side 10 cm and resistance 0.5 Ω is in a uniform field of 0.10 T at 45° to its normal. The field is reduced steadily to zero in 0.70 s. Find the induced emf and current.

problem.en: A coil of 100 turns and area 0.02 m² has its plane perpendicular to a field that falls from 0.5 T to 0.1 T in 0.2 s. Find the average induced emf.

steps.en: ΔΦ per turn = ΔB × A = 0.4 × 0.02 = 8 × 10⁻³ Wb.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A coil of 100 turns and area 0.02 m² has its plane perpendicular to a field that falls from 0.5 T to 0.1 T in 0.2 s. Find the average induced emf.

heading.en: Induced charge does not depend on time

body.en: Total charge driven round a coil of resistance R is Q = NΔΦ/R. Whether you pull the magnet out fast or slowly, the same charge flows; only the current and emf change.

narration.en: Induced charge does not depend on time. Total charge driven round a coil of resistance R is Q = NΔΦ/R. Whether you pull the magnet out fast or slowly, the same charge flows; only the current and emf change.

narration.kn: ತಂಡ ರಸಪ್ರಶ್ನೆ. ಪ್ರತಿ ತಂಡವು ಮೆಲ್ಲನೆ ಚರ್ಚಿಸಿ ಒಂದು ಉತ್ತರ ನೀಡಲಿ.

points.en: Φ = BA cos θ, in weber.
A changing flux induces an emf; a steady flux does not.
points.kn: ಬದಲಾಗುವ ಅಭಿವಾಹ ವಿ.ಚಾ.ಬ. ಉಂಟುಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ; ಸ್ಥಿರ ಅಭಿವಾಹ ಮಾಡುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.

homework.en: A 200-turn coil of area 0.01 m² is turned in 0.1 s from perpendicular to parallel with a field of 0.2 T. Find the average emf.

narration.en: Recap. Φ = BA cos θ, in weber. A changing flux induces an emf; a steady flux does not. Faraday's law: ε = −N dΦ/dt.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. Φ = BA cosθ, ವೆಬರ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ. ಬದಲಾಗುವ ಅಭಿವಾಹ ವಿ.ಚಾ.ಬ. ಉಂಟುಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ; ಸ್ಥಿರ ಅಭಿವಾಹ ಮಾಡುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ಫ್ಯಾರಡೆ ನಿಯಮ: ε = −N dΦ/dt.
